entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jacopo Passavanti (c. 1280-1357) was a pivotal figure in the Dominican Order during the Late Medieval period.

As an Italian preacher and writer, Jacopo played a crucial role in shaping the theological landscape of his time. His works, which often focused on moral instruction and spiritual guidance, have been preserved through various translations and manuscripts. This has allowed scholars to gain insight into the intellectual currents of 14th-century Europe, where Passavanti operated.

His legacy extends beyond the realm of theology; as a Dominican friar, Jacopo was deeply involved in the social and charitable activities characteristic of his Order. He contributed to various community initiatives, including education and healthcare programs, which helped to improve the lives of marginalized groups within urban centers like Bologna and Siena.

One lasting impact of Passavanti's work can be seen in the enduring relevance of his theological treatises, many of which continue to influence contemporary Christian thought. This testament to his intellectual influence underscores the significance of Passavanti as a key figure in the evolution of medieval spirituality.

The sheer volume of manuscripts bearing Passavanti's name serves as a poignant reminder of the immense cultural impact he had during this period. From humble beginnings as an Italian Dominican friar, Jacopo Passavanti left behind an indelible mark on Western religious thought and practice.
